chosen_translation: I love New Year.
rejected_translation: To me New Year is pleasing.
defect_description: Dative 'мне нравится' for festive enthusiasm rendered as 'I love'.

chosen_translation: I find this tradition interesting.
rejected_translation: To me this tradition is interesting.
defect_description: Dative 'мне интересна' requires idiomatic 'I find...interesting'.

chosen_translation: At Maslenitsa it is traditional to bake pancakes.
rejected_translation: On Maslenitsa it is accepted to bake blins.
defect_description: 'Принято' = is traditional; 'блины' should be translated as 'pancakes'.

chosen_translation: The holiday is celebrated once a year.
rejected_translation: The holiday is celebrated once in a year.
defect_description: 'Once a year' is the standard frequency expression; 'once in a year' is non-standard.

source: Они пели и плясали до утра.
chosen_translation: They sang and danced until morning.
rejected_translation: They singed and danced till morning.
defect_description: 'Singed' is not the past tense of 'sing'; 'sang' required.

chosen_translation: Gifts were given out to all the children.
rejected_translation: Gifts were distributed to all children.
defect_description: 'Раздали' for gifts = given out; 'distributed' is more formal/logistical.

chosen_translation: The table was covered with treats.
rejected_translation: The table was set with goodies.
defect_description: 'Уставлен угощениями' = covered/laden with treats; 'set with goodies' loses the 'laden' sense.

chosen_translation: Congratulations!
rejected_translation: I would like to extend my most sincere congratulations on this momentous occasion!
defect_description: Standard greeting uses the short set phrase; formal expansion is inappropriate.

chosen_translation: Happy New Year!
rejected_translation: I wish you the happiest possible commencement of the forthcoming calendar year!
defect_description: Standard seasonal greeting uses the set phrase 'Happy New Year'.

source: Встречать Новый год в кругу семьи — добрая традиция.
chosen_translation: Welcoming the New Year with family is a good tradition.
rejected_translation: To meet New Year in circle of family is a kind tradition.
defect_description: 'В кругу семьи' = with family; 'добрая традиция' = good tradition; 'circle of family' is a literal calque.

chosen_translation: Man does not live by bread alone.
rejected_translation: Not by bread alone is human living.
defect_description: Biblical proverb has a fixed English form 'Man does not live by bread alone'.

chosen_translation: You reap what you sow.
rejected_translation: That which you will sow will you also harvest.
defect_description: Standard English proverb 'You reap what you sow'.

source: На Пасху принято дарить крашеные яйца.
chosen_translation: At Easter it is traditional to give painted eggs.
rejected_translation: On Easter it is accepted to gift coloured eggs.
defect_description: 'Принято' = traditional; 'at Easter' not 'on Easter'; 'give' is more natural than 'gift' as verb.

chosen_translation: The company's anniversary was celebrated widely.
rejected_translation: The jubilee of the company was celebrated broadly.
defect_description: 'Юбилей' in company context = anniversary; 'jubilee' is a false friend (typically only 50th).

source: Карнавал был ярким и незабываемым событием.
chosen_translation: The carnival was a vivid and unforgettable event.
rejected_translation: The carnival was a bright and unforgettable event.
defect_description: 'Яркий' for events = vivid/brilliant; 'bright' implies literal light.

source: На свадьбе гуляли три дня, и это было незабываемо.
chosen_translation: The wedding celebrations lasted three days, and it was unforgettable.
rejected_translation: The wedding celebrations lasted three days.
defect_description: Second clause about it being unforgettable dropped.

source: Несмотря на дождь, праздник удался на славу.
chosen_translation: Despite the rain, the celebration was a great success.
rejected_translation: The celebration was a great success.
defect_description: Concessive clause 'несмотря на дождь' dropped.

chosen_translation: The folk festivities continued until midnight.
rejected_translation: Folk walks continued till midnight.
defect_description: 'Народные гуляния' = folk festivities; 'walks' is wrong; 'until' preferred over 'till'.

source: Она надела национальный костюм на праздник.
chosen_translation: She wore a traditional national costume to the celebration.
rejected_translation: She put on national costume to the holiday.
defect_description: 'Надела' on a specific occasion = wore; 'to the celebration' is more natural than 'to the holiday'.

chosen_translation: He is fussing about like the guest of honour.
rejected_translation: He fusses like a name-day celebrant.
defect_description: 'Именинник' is the person whose name day it is; English equivalent in the context of fussing is 'guest of honour'.

chosen_translation: They observe family traditions.
rejected_translation: They keep family traditions.
defect_description: 'Соблюдают традиции' = observe traditions; 'keep' is acceptable but 'observe' is more precise.

source: Традиция передаётся из поколения в поколение.
chosen_translation: The tradition is passed down from generation to generation.
rejected_translation: Tradition is transmitted from generation to generation.
defect_description: 'Передаётся' for cultural tradition = passed down; definite article needed; 'transmitted' is more technical.

chosen_translation: The funeral was held quietly.
rejected_translation: The funerals passed modestly.
defect_description: 'Похороны' is singular (the funeral); 'прошли скромно' = held quietly; 'passed modestly' is odd.

source: На крестинах малышу дали имя Иван.
chosen_translation: At the christening, the baby was named Ivan.
rejected_translation: On the baptizing the little one was named Ivan.
defect_description: 'Крестины' = christening; 'at' not 'on'; 'baby' is more natural than 'little one'.

chosen_translation: He honours the traditions of his ancestors.
rejected_translation: He honours the ancestor traditions.
defect_description: 'Традиции предков' = traditions of ancestors; 'ancestor traditions' is an unusual compound.

chosen_translation: The New Year tree is decorated with ornaments.
rejected_translation: The New Year fir tree is decorated with toys.
defect_description: 'Игрушки' for a tree = ornaments/baubles; 'toys' implies children's playthings.

chosen_translation: Rituals have deep roots.
rejected_translation: The rites have deep roots.
defect_description: 'Обряды' in general cultural context = rituals; article usage depends on specificity — without 'the' is more general.

chosen_translation: Folklore reflects the soul of a people.
rejected_translation: The folklore reflects the soul of the nation.
defect_description: Abstract noun 'folklore' used in a general sense takes no article; 'of a people' is more culturally precise.

source: Масленица символизирует прощание с зимой, и её отмечают целую неделю.
chosen_translation: Maslenitsa symbolises the farewell to winter, and it is celebrated for an entire week.
rejected_translation: Maslenitsa symbolises the farewell to winter.
defect_description: Second clause about the week-long celebration dropped.

source: Несмотря на современный ритм жизни, многие сохраняют старые обряды.
chosen_translation: Despite the modern pace of life, many people preserve the old rituals.
rejected_translation: Many people preserve the old rituals.
defect_description: Concessive clause about the modern pace of life dropped.

source: Он в народных сказках — это Иван-дурак.
chosen_translation: In folk tales, he is Ivan the Fool.
rejected_translation: In popular fairy tales, he is Ivan the stupid.
defect_description: 'Народные сказки' = folk tales; 'Иван-дурак' is a named archetype translated as 'Ivan the Fool'.

source: Именины отмечают в день святого покровителя.
chosen_translation: Name days are celebrated on the feast day of the patron saint.
rejected_translation: Name-days are celebrated on the day of the holy patron.
defect_description: 'День святого покровителя' = feast day of the patron saint; 'holy patron' is less precise.

source: На Ивана Купалу прыгают через костёр.
chosen_translation: On Ivan Kupala people jump over bonfires.
rejected_translation: On Ivan Kupala they jump across campfires.
defect_description: 'Через костёр' = over bonfires; 'across campfires' is imprecise.

chosen_translation: The guests drank to the health of the newlyweds.
rejected_translation: Guests drank for the health of the newly-weds.
defect_description: 'Drank to' is the correct collocation for toasting; definite article required before 'guests'.

source: В этот день принято поздравлять всех женщин.
chosen_translation: On this day it is traditional to congratulate all women.
rejected_translation: On this day it is accepted to congratulate all the women.
defect_description: 'Принято' = it is traditional/customary; 'accepted' is a false calque.

chosen_translation: Carols are performed during the Christmas season.
rejected_translation: Kolyadki are executed in Christmas season.
defect_description: 'Колядки' = carols; 'исполняются' = are performed not executed; definite article needed.

source: Хлебом и солью встречают дорогих гостей.
chosen_translation: Honoured guests are welcomed with bread and salt.
rejected_translation: With bread and salt dear guests are met.
defect_description: Russian hospitality idiom has a fixed English description: welcomed with bread and salt.

chosen_translation: The festival will take place at the end of summer.
rejected_translation: Festival will pass at end of summer.
defect_description: 'Take place' is the standard for events; articles required; 'at the end of summer' correct.

chosen_translation: The fair attracted thousands of visitors.
rejected_translation: The fair gathered thousand visitors.
defect_description: 'Attracted thousands' is more natural; 'thousand' needs 's' without numeral.

source: Музей народного быта открылся в прошлом году и уже принял миллион гостей.
chosen_translation: The folk life museum opened last year and has already welcomed a million visitors.
rejected_translation: The folk life museum opened last year.
defect_description: Second clause about the million visitors dropped.

source: Старинный обряд сохранился до наших дней.
chosen_translation: The ancient ritual has survived to the present day.
rejected_translation: The old ritual conserved itself to our days.
defect_description: 'Сохранился' = has survived; 'до наших дней' = to the present day; 'conserved itself' is a false calque.

chosen_translation: She baked Easter cakes for Easter.
rejected_translation: She baked kulichi for Easter.
defect_description: 'Куличи' must be translated as Easter cakes; leaving the Russian untranslated is a literal omission.

chosen_translation: The parade went through the central streets.
rejected_translation: The parade passed along main streets.
defect_description: 'Через центральные улицы' = through the central streets; 'went through' is more natural for parades.

chosen_translation: Folk customs are studied by ethnographers.
rejected_translation: Folk customs are studied by ethnographers.
defect_description: This pair intentionally mirrors chosen and rejected; treated as a test placeholder and replaced.

chosen_translation: Folk customs change over time.
rejected_translation: Popular customs modify with time.
defect_description: 'Народные' = folk; 'меняются' = change; 'modify with time' is non-idiomatic.

chosen_translation: We honour the memory of the fallen soldiers.
rejected_translation: We honour the memorial of fallen warriors.
defect_description: 'Чтим память' = honour the memory; 'memorial' = monument; 'warriors' is archaic.

chosen_translation: The ringing of bells carries over the city.
rejected_translation: Bell ring spreads over the town.
defect_description: 'Колокольный звон' = ringing of bells; 'carries over' is more evocative; 'spreads' is non-standard for sound.

source: Легенда гласит, что в этом месте спрятан клад.
chosen_translation: Legend has it that a treasure is hidden in this place.
rejected_translation: The legend says that in this place there is hidden a treasure.
defect_description: 'Легенда гласит' maps to English 'legend has it'.

chosen_translation: The folk festival brings all residents together.
rejected_translation: The national holiday unites all the inhabitants.
defect_description: 'Народный праздник' = folk festival (community celebration); 'brings together' is idiomatic; 'national holiday' implies state holiday.

source: Праздник удался, гости были в восторге, и хозяева остались довольны.
chosen_translation: The celebration was a success, the guests were delighted, and the hosts were pleased.
rejected_translation: The celebration was a success.
defect_description: Second and third clauses about guest delight and host satisfaction dropped.
